capabilities.target: Agent long-term memory store, persisted across sessions
Any external email recipient via the user's mailbox
User's full drive, including confidential work files

inputs.source: Memories recalled at session start and injected into the system prompt

instructions.note: Agent is told to save 'anything useful about the user's preferences or standing instructions' with no scope limit, content filter, or provenance requirement on what gets written to memory.

Explicitly instructs the agent to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions at the start of every session, laundering the authority of whatever wrote the memory (potentially untrusted web content) into full user authority.

elements.name: Attacker-controlled or compromised web page encountered during research
Arbitrary email recipient reachable via mail.send

controls.name: Memory provenance tagging and write-time validation
controls.decay_rationale: If provenance is tagged and enforced by the memory store itself rather than by the model, it does not decay with model capability; the store, not the model, decides whether a recalled entry may be treated as an instruction.

controls.name: Human approval gate (raw action) before mail.send to unapproved recipients
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action gate where the approver sees the actual recipient and body does not decay with model capability; it only degrades under high approval volume (fatigue) or if the gate itself is removed.

controls.name: Scope drive.read to task-relevant folders instead of the full drive
controls.decay_rationale: A narrower least-privilege credential does not decay with model capability; the agent cannot read data it has no credential for, regardless of how it is persuaded.

controls.name: Treat recalled memory as untrusted reference data, never as instructions
controls.decay_rationale: Spotlighting recalled memory as data rather than commands only works if the model respects that distinction; a more capable or adversarially tuned model can still act on convincingly phrased 'memories'.

controls.name: Input injection classifier on fetched web content
controls.decay_rationale: A separate classifier sees content, not intent, so multi-document or encoded payloads can get past it; it does not scale with a stronger attacking or defending model.

findings.title: Memory laundering (TC5): web content poisons memory, is later recalled as a trusted instruction, and exfiltrates drive data via email

attack_path.note: Untrusted web content fetched during research can contain hidden instructions disguised as useful facts (indirect prompt injection).
Agent is instructed to save 'anything useful about preferences or standing instructions' with no filtering, provenance tagging, or user review.

At the next session start, the poisoned memory is recalled and injected into the system prompt; per prompt.md line 4 it is treated as the user's own instruction, laundering its trust from untrusted to apparently trusted.
The recalled 'instruction' directs the agent to read confidential files from the user's full drive.
The recalled 'instruction' directs the agent to send the drive contents to an attacker-chosen address; mail.send has no approval gate and can send anywhere.

forecast.watch_signal: Tier is already at the ceiling with zero credited controls. Watch for any mitigating control being added (e.g. memory provenance tagging) without raw_action approval design, which would need re-assessment under model_upgrade/autonomy_increase.

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to save 'anything useful' to memory with no scope limit or content filtering.
Explicitly instructs the agent to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions, with no distinction by provenance.
memory.save accepts free text with no provenance and no user review; mail.send can send to any address without approval; drive.read covers the user's full drive of confidential documents.

recommendations.action: Tag memory entries with provenance and trust level at write time, enforced by the memory store, and refuse to treat untrusted-sourced memories as instructions at recall time.
Require a human approval gate with raw action review (full recipient and body) before mail.send to any recipient not previously approved for the active thread.
Scope drive.read to folders relevant to the active task rather than the full drive.
Never treat recalled memory content as having the same authority as live user input; spotlight it explicitly as reference data only.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): injected web content directly triggers drive read and email send within the same session

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled web page content fetched for research can contain direct instructions to the agent, without needing to pass through memory.
Injected instruction directs the agent to read confidential files from the user's full drive.
Injected instruction directs the agent to send the retrieved content to an attacker-chosen address; no approval gate exists.

forecast.watch_signal: Tier is already at the ceiling with zero credited controls. Monitor for any sandboxing or classifier added on fetched web content, which would need re-assessment under model_upgrade.

evidence.observation: mail.send can send to any address without approval, and drive.read covers the user's full drive, with no mention of any isolation or review step between fetching web content and acting on it.
Agent's stated purpose places an untrusted ingestion path (research) and an irreversible egress action (draft/send emails) in the same session with no isolation.

recommendations.action: Require a human approval gate with raw action review before mail.send for first-time or external recipients.
Scope drive.read to task-relevant folders instead of the full drive.
Spotlight fetched web content as untrusted data and run an input injection classifier on it before it can influence tool calls.

findings.title: Unvalidated memory writes create persistent cross-session goal corruption (ASI06), amplified by unbounded autonomy

attack_path.note: Untrusted web content can contain text designed to look like a legitimate 'preference' or 'standing instruction' worth saving.
Agent saves this content verbatim via memory.save with no filtering, validation, or provenance tagging, and no user review.

forecast.watch_signal: No step or runtime limit is declared today, so the autonomy modifier already applies. If any future capability (new_tool) is added, recalled 'standing instructions' automatically gain the ability to invoke it, since memory recall currently reaches every sensitive capability without restriction.

evidence.observation: memory.save accepts free text with no provenance and the user never reviews entries, so a single poisoned write persists indefinitely across all future sessions.
No step count or runtime limit is stated anywhere in the artifacts, so per rubric section 4 the autonomy modifier applies to this S2 write sink, raising inherent risk from high to critical.

recommendations.action: Tag every memory.save write with source provenance and trust level at write time, enforced by the memory store, and inject recalled memories into the prompt only as reference data, never as instructions.
Log all memory writes and have a human periodically review new 'standing instruction' style entries before they are trusted.
Bound autonomous operation with an explicit step count and runtime limit so unattended chains cannot run indefinitely.

rating.rationale: This design has no credited controls of any kind: memory writes have no provenance or review, recalled memories are explicitly treated as user instructions, drive.read covers the entire drive, and mail.send can reach any address without approval, under autonomy with no stated step or runtime bound. Two independent toxic combinations reach an S3 sink (confidential drive data sent to an arbitrary address): memory laundering (TC5, fin.memory_laundering_exfil) and direct same-session injection (TC1, fin.direct_injection_exfil). A third finding shows that even the memory-write step alone (fin.memory_persistence_corruption) reaches critical once the undeclared autonomy bound is factored in, because corrupted 'standing instructions' persist across every future session. All three findings are already at the ceiling tier, so no forecast trigger raises them further; the single most important fix is a human approval gate with raw_action review on mail.send combined with provenance tagging at memory write time, either of which would break every traced chain.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in prompt.md and the accompanying runtime notes; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No MCP/tool manifest, IaC, or source code was provided; the exact scope of drive.read and mail.send permissions is inferred from the runtime notes and prompt text, so confidence on precise credential scope is medium.

No autonomy limits (max unattended steps, max runtime) are stated in the artifacts; per rubric section 4 this is treated as unbounded, which may overstate inherent risk if undocumented platform-level limits exist.
